text:
Christian Dvorak plays the minutes nobody envies on a Flyers team that has won rarely. He's averaging nearly 18 minutes a night, up over 18 and a half in his last ten, and Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 97th percentile last season. That context matters when you see the five-on-five numbers: Philadelphia gets only 41% of the expected goals with him on the ice.

The scoring has picked up as the role grew. Seven of his 11 points came in the last ten games, including two assists in the win over Vancouver on November 9. His goals (3 on 3.9 expected) are a touch light, nothing dramatic.

What we'd watch is whether his line can stop bleeding chances. A shutdown center can live with modest offense, but not with being outshot this badly, and the Flyers don't have much room to absorb it. He's 30, steady, and probably more valuable in a lighter role than the one this roster needs from him.
headline: Dvorak is carrying the tough minutes
